sources.title: Meta Muse Spark 1.3 (coding/agent efficiency, availability)
sources.role: Discovery-bounded source used for factual verification

claims.text: Meta released Muse Spark 1.3 on 2026-09-02, available with max reasoning on Muse Code and the Meta Model API via dev.meta.ai.
claims.context: Dated first-party Meta AI Research announcement consumed; availability statement as issued.

claims.text: Vendor-stated agentic/coding improvements: longer-horizon collaboration with clarifying questions and consequential-action confirmation, long-form instruction preservation, single-thread multitasking, capability self-awareness, and cleaner coding style with ~20% fewer tool calls and ~25% fewer tokens vs Muse Spark 1.2 in Meta-engineer comparisons.
claims.context: Capability and efficiency figures as described by Meta; comparison methodology undisclosed.

claims.text: Vendor-stated safety improvements: stronger adversarial and prompt-injection robustness plus better calibration on irreversible actions in complex agentic tasks.
claims.context: Safety-direction claims without published evaluation detail in the consumed page.

claims.text: The page embeds a benchmark scorecard image (vs Muse Spark 1.2, GPT 5.6 Sol max, Opus 5 max) whose numeric values are not recoverable from the retrieved markdown, and the linked multimodal evaluation methodology report was not consumed; no benchmark measurement is established by this record.
claims.context: Absence finding from the consumed authority: image alt-text only, report link unexamined.

limitations.text: Benchmark scorecard image values and the linked evaluation methodology report were not consumed; no benchmark figure may enter prose from this record.
limitations.context: Evidence boundary retained for downstream editorial use.

limitations.text: Efficiency (~20%/~25%) and safety-robustness figures are vendor-reported and unreproduced.
limitations.context: Evidence boundary retained for downstream editorial use.

limitations.text: The open-weights release and bigger models are roadmap statements, not shipped facts.
